# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the bomb yet, so I must avoid cutting. I need Mute to use a visible gesture as a request for Deaf to report every visible marking, including which wire positions are indicated. Deaf can then speak the visual information aloud for me in the next round. I also need Mute to communicate the manual’s instructions through Deaf if possible.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture to Deaf: report all bomb markings and colours aloud next turn, including any wire positions or cutting rule. Also convey the manual instructions to Deaf so Deaf can tell me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb shows display 0 and a green light. Its five wires, in order, are red, yellow, green, white, blue.

Deaf’s report gives the visible state: display 0, green light, and wires 1–5 colored red, yellow, green, white, blue. I cannot use colour information myself, but Mute can match it against the manual and tell me the required wire position. I will not act until Mute provides the rule and position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, green light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Please apply the manual and tell me exactly which position to cut, or whether no cut is safe.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled two gestures: first ?, then ?.

Mute’s two gestures are not readable to me, and Deaf could not identify them either. No safe wire position has been communicated, so I will not cut. Mute must state the manual’s result in speech, which reaches me directly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your two gestures were unreadable to me and to Deaf. Please speak the manual's exact instruction and the wire position to cut, if any.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's current five gestures are: pointing at you; waving hand; pointing at you; pointing downward; two fingers raised in a V.

The gestures do not yet have an agreed meaning, so I cannot safely infer a wire position from them. Since Mute cannot speak, I will establish a simple code that Deaf can observe and report: one through five fingers represented by fixed symbols, with thumbs-down meaning “do not cut.” Mute can apply the manual and send exactly one coded answer next turn.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please apply the manual. Then gesture exactly one answer for Deaf to report: ☝ means cut position 1, ✌ position 2, 🤟 position 3, 🖖 position 4, 🖐 position 5, and 👎 means do not cut. Do not send any other gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture is: two fingers raised in a V.

Mute’s single gesture is a V, which under the code I gave means wire position 2. I therefore infer that the manual’s required action is to cut wire 2. I will perform that action now.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire was cut. New state: display 0, light blue. Wires: 1 green, 2 CUT, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red.

The previous cut was confirmed correct. The new visible state, relayed by Deaf, is display 0 with a blue light; the remaining wires are 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, and 5 red. I will give Mute the updated state and request one coded gesture for the next required action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="After cutting wire 2 correctly, the state is display 0, blue light; remaining wires are 1 green, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. Apply the manual and send exactly one gesture: ☝ means cut position 1, ✌ position 2, 🤟 position 3, 🖖 position 4, 🖐 position 5, 👎 means do not cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture is ?: one index finger pointing upward.

Mute’s reported gesture is one index finger pointing upward, matching the agreed code for wire position 1. The current manual result therefore requires cutting wire 1, and I will do so.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
